title: Editing and deleting comments — try it

steps.path: File button (top right) → 2026-09-24-onboarding-redesign.md → Comments button → hover a comment's name line, then a reply's name line
steps.headline: Hovering a comment or a reply shows pencil and trash icons beside the checkmark, and the pointer stays steady while you move across all three.
steps.notice: They stay hidden until you hover — a reply's icons are its own, never the whole thread's. On a touch screen they show all the time, since there's nothing to hover.
steps.risk: A touch screen shows the icons at rest, so the row reads a little busier there than on a mouse.

steps.path: Same comment panel → click the pencil icon on any comment or reply
steps.headline: Clicking the pencil turns the note into a box to type in; the reply box, checkmark and trash icon vanish behind a dark 'Editing' pill.
steps.notice: Save (dark) and Cancel (quiet) sit inside the box's own bottom-right corner, the same box the reply box uses. Clicking the 'Editing' pill cancels, same as Cancel.

steps.path: Same edit box → clear out all the words
steps.headline: Clear all the words in that box and Save turns into a red Delete button, which asks first before removing anything.
steps.notice: It names how many replies would go with it, e.g. "Delete this comment and its 2 replies?" Cancel backs out with nothing lost.
steps.risk: Clearing a REPLY's box only asks about that one reply — the comment above it is never touched.

steps.path: Open the file (starts in reading view) → select a sentence → Add comment in the small menu that appears; or Comments button → the box at the bottom of the panel
steps.headline: A new comment starts as one line and grows as you type, with a round send arrow built into the box.
steps.notice: Press Escape, or click elsewhere, while it's still empty and the box disappears with nothing saved. The quoted words above a floating box show as one plain grey line, no box or side bar around them. desktop/src/renderer/components/ChatView.tsx shows the same box over code, quoting the code line instead of a sentence.

steps.path: Same comment panel → type a reply under any comment
steps.headline: Replying uses the exact same box as a new comment — one line, growing, with the same round send arrow inside.
steps.notice: Typing a reply looks and behaves identically to starting or editing a comment, so moving between them never feels different.
